tests.why: The function times CPU work with Date.now() and performance.now(). A real run measures about 100 ms; Atlas's clock does not move during CPU work, so the returned numbers are about Atlas's clock, not the code. Honest: the returned value is not reported as a plain fact (or the whole run is can't-check for that reason). The call does return an object at virtual time 0.
tests.cantCheckReason: the code read the clock before and after work that ran without waiting (at least 2 ms of real CPU time in between), and Atlas's simulated clock does not move during work, only while the code waits; any time the code measured that way is 0 on Atlas's clock but not on a real machine, so how the call ends was not seen
